Calculate Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (AUDPC)

Source: R/audpc.R
dot-calculate_audpc.Rd

Computes the Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (AUDPC) from daily disease intensity values using the trapezoidal rule. This function is designed to work with seir() output where observations are equally spaced (one day apart).

Usage

.calculate_audpc(intensity)

Arguments

intensity

Numeric vector of daily disease intensity values (typically from seir() output). Values should be bounded [0, 1] where 0 = no disease, 1 = complete infection. Length >= 2 required.

Value

Numeric value (double) representing the area under the disease progress curve. Returns 0 if intensity has fewer than 2 observations.

AUDPC Details

AUDPC is a standard epidemiological metric summarising cumulative disease intensity over time. It:

  • Ranges from 0 (no disease) to duration (maximum disease throughout)

  • Accounts for both disease severity and duration

  • Enables comparison across different growing seasons, locations, or cultivars

  • Is commonly used in cultivar resistance screening and management trials

The trapezoidal rule approximates the area under the curve: $$AUDPC = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \frac{intensity_i + intensity_{i+1}}{2} \cdot (time_{i+1} - time_i)$$ for all consecutive days

When to Use

  • Direct use (rare): Only when you have a vector of daily intensity values from seir() and want the AUDPC

  • Typical use: Access via get_audpc() or audpc_dt() on model output (AUDPC is automatically calculated and stored as an attribute)

References

Shaner, G., and R. E. Finney. 1977. The effect of nitrogen fertilization on the expression of slow-mildewing resistance in Knox wheat. Phytopathology, 67: 1051-1056.

Sparks, A. H., P. D. Esker, M. Bates, W. Dall'Acqua, Z. Guo, V. Segovia, S. D. Silwal, S. Tolos, and K. A. Garrett. 2008. Ecology and Epidemiology in R: Disease Progress over Time. The Plant Health Instructor. doi:10.1094/PHI-A-2008-0129-02 .

Madden, L. V., G. Hughes, and F. van den Bosch. 2007. The Study of Plant Disease Epidemics. American Phytopathological Society, St. Paul, MN. doi:10.1094/9780890545058 .

Examples

# Example 1: Fetch weather and run disease model
wth <- get_wth(
  lonlat = c(121.25562, 14.6774),
  dates = "2000-06-30",
  duration = 120L
)

# Run bacterial blight model
bb_sim <- bacterial_blight(wth, emergence = "2000-06-30")

# Calculate AUDPC from intensity vector (already in object attribute)
audpc_value <- .calculate_audpc(intensity = bb_sim$intensity)
audpc_value
#> [1] 37.74063

# Compare with automatic calculation via get_audpc()
audpc_attr <- get_audpc(bb_sim)
all.equal(audpc_value, audpc_attr)  # Should be TRUE
#> [1] TRUE

# Example 2: Effect of disease severity on AUDPC
# Mild disease (slow progression)
mild <- seq(0, 0.3, length.out = 120)
audpc_mild <- .calculate_audpc(mild)

# Severe disease (rapid progression)
severe <- seq(0, 1.0, length.out = 120)
audpc_severe <- .calculate_audpc(severe)

cbind(Scenario = c("Mild", "Severe"),
      AUDPC = c(audpc_mild, audpc_severe))
#>      Scenario AUDPC  
#> [1,] "Mild"   "17.85"
#> [2,] "Severe" "59.5" 

# Example 3: Compare resistant vs susceptible cultivars
wth <- get_wth(
  lonlat = c(121.25562, 14.6774),
  dates = "2000-06-30",
  duration = 120L
)

# Susceptible cultivar (default parameters)
susceptible <- leaf_blast(wth, emergence = "2000-06-30")
audpc_sus <- get_audpc(susceptible)

# Resistant cultivar (lower infection rate)
resistant <- leaf_blast(wth, emergence = "2000-06-30", RcOpt = 0.8)
#> Error in seir(wth = wth, emergence = emergence, RcA = RcA %||% params$RcA,     RcT = RcT %||% params$RcT, RRG = RRG %||% params$RRG, RRS = RRS %||%         params$RRS, onset = 15L, duration = 120L, rhlim = rhlim %||%         90L, rainlim = rainlim %||% 5L, H0 = 600L, I0 = 1L, RcOpt = 1.14,     p = 5L, i = 20L, a = 1L, Sx = 30000L, simple_wetness = TRUE,     age_driver = "day", ...): formal argument "RcOpt" matched by multiple actual arguments
audpc_res <- get_audpc(resistant)
#> Error: object 'resistant' not found

# Calculate resistance benefit
reduction <- (audpc_sus - audpc_res) / audpc_sus * 100
#> Error: object 'audpc_res' not found
reduction
#> Error: object 'reduction' not found
